segments.arabic: [1011] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا زائدة قال: حدثنا زياد بن علاقة قال: سمعت المغيرة بن شعبة يقول
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us. He said: Ziyad ibn ‘Ilaqah related to us. He said: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah saying:

segments.arabic: انكسفت الشمس يوم مات إبراهيم، فقال الناس انكسفت لموت إبراهيم، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: إن الشمس والقمر آيتان من آيات الله لا ينكسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتموهما فادعوا الله وصلوا حتى ينجلي
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim died. The people said: “It was eclipsed because of Ibrahim’s death.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see them, supplicate to Allah and pray until it clears.”

comparisons.note: The signs clause, death and life, both concluding instructions and until it clears remain. The Bewley web comparison omits the signs clause and the until-clearing ending. The Khan body retains them but adds an explanatory identification of Ibrahim that is not inserted into the report.

segments.arabic: [1012] وقال أبو أسامة حدثنا هشام قال: أخبرتني فاطمة بنت المنذر عن أسماء قالت
segments.english: And Abu Usamah said: Hisham related to us. He said: Fatimah bint al-Mundhir informed me, from Asma’, who said:

segments.arabic: فانصرف رسول الله ﷺ وقد تجلت الشمس فخطب فحمد الله بما هو أهله، ثم قال: أما بعد
segments.english: Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, and the sun had cleared. He delivered an address and praised Allah as He deserves. Then he said: “To proceed.”

segments.arabic: [1013] حدثنا محمود قال: حدثنا سعيد بن عامر عن شعبة عن يونس عن الحسن عن أبي بكرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Mahmud related to us. He said: Sa‘id ibn ‘Amir related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: انكسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فصلى ركعتين
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he prayed two rak‘ahs.

notes: This brief Abu Bakrah account retains its own complete chain and the selected Most High honorific. Brill expands Mahmud with ibn Ghaylan, calls the Prophet rather than the Messenger in the report, and omits Abu Bakrah’s honorific. The modern print has the shorter companion honorific without Most High. These print variants do not replace selected wording.

The source chapter names a lunar eclipse while this report itself names the sun. Both are retained exactly in their separate roles; the heading does not authorize changing the report to the moon or merging it with the following account.

segments.arabic: [1014] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا يونس عن الحسن عن أبي بكرة قال
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Yunus related to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said:

segments.arabic: خسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فخرج يجر رداءه حتى انتهى إلى المسجد وثاب الناس إليه فصلى بهم ركعتين فانجلت الشمس،
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He went out dragging his cloak until he reached the mosque. The people gathered around him, and he led them in two rak‘ahs. Then the sun cleared.

segments.arabic: فقال إن الشمس والقمر آيتان من آيات الله وإنهما لا يخسفان لموت أحد وإذا كان ذاك فصلوا وادعوا حتى يكشف ما بكم
segments.english: He said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death. When that happens, pray and supplicate until what has come upon you is removed.”

segments.arabic: وذاك أن ابنا للنبي ﷺ مات يقال له إبراهيم، فقال الناس في ذاك
segments.english: That was because a son of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had died, called Ibrahim, and the people spoke about that.

comparisons.note: The sun clearing after the prayer and before the speech remains explicit. segments.arabic: [1015] حدثنا محمود قال: حدثنا أبو أحمد قال: حدثنا سفيان عن يحيى عن عمرة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Mahmud related to us. He said: Abu Ahmad related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Amrah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ صلى بهم في كسوف الشمس أربع ركعات في سجدتين الأول الأول أطول
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led them in the solar eclipse prayer with four bowings in two rak‘ahs; the first, the first was longer.

notes: The working English renders arba rakat fi sajdatayn as four bowings in two rakahs. Ibn al-Mulaqqin explicitly explains the use of sajdah for a whole rakah here; both located English comparisons use this count. This terminology explanation stays in the source notes rather than becoming new report wording.

The selected ending repeats al-awwal al-awwal. The English repeats the first, the first rather than silently adopting Brill’s shorter al-ula ending or either English comparison’s shortened ending. Commentary discusses the earlier and later prayer portions; no detailed prayer sequence is inserted. Independent lexical review remains pending.

Brill expands Mahmud with ibn Ghaylan and both prints have the shorter Aishah honorific without Most High. The selected source has Amrah, not Urwah, in this chain. The report says he led them; the English comparisons’ us is not imported.

segments.arabic: [1016] حدثنا محمد بن مهران قال: حدثنا الوليد قال: أخبرنا ابن نمر سمع ابن شهاب عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Mihran related to us. He said: al-Walid related to us. He said: Ibn Namir informed us; he heard Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: جهر النبي ﷺ في صلاة الخسوف بقراءته فإذا فرغ من قراءته كبر فركع وإذا رفع من الركعة قال سمع الله لمن حمده ربنا ولك الحمد ثم يعاود القراءة في صلاة الكسوف أربع ركعات في ركعتين وأربع سجدات،
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited aloud in the eclipse prayer. When he finished his recitation, he proclaimed Allah’s greatness and bowed. When he rose from the bowing, he said: “Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” Then he resumed recitation. In the eclipse prayer there were four bowings in two rak‘ahs and four prostrations.

segments.arabic: وقال الأوزاعي وغيره سمعت الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Al-Awza‘i and others said: I heard al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that:

segments.arabic: أن الشمس خسفت على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فبعث مناديا ب الصلاة جامعة فتقدم فصلى أربع ركعات في ركعتين وأربع سجدات
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He sent a caller to announce: “Prayer in congregation.” Then he went forward and prayed four bowings in two rak‘ahs and four prostrations.

segments.arabic: وأخبرني عبد الرحمن بن نمر سمع ابن شهاب مثله
segments.english: And ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Namir informed me that he heard the same from Ibn Shihab.

segments.arabic: قال الزهري فقلت: ما صنع أخوك ذلك عبد الله بن الزبير ما صلى إلا ركعتين مثل الصبح إذ صلى بالمدينة قال أجل إنه أخطأ السنة
segments.english: Al-Zuhri said: I said: “Your brother, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, did not do that. He prayed only two rak‘ahs, like the dawn prayer, when he prayed in Madinah.” He said: “Yes, he was mistaken about the Sunnah.”

segments.arabic: تابعه سفيان بن حسين وسليمان بن كثير عن الزهري في الجهر
segments.english: Sufyan ibn Husayn and Sulayman ibn Kathir followed him in transmitting from al-Zuhri about reciting aloud.

checkedBody: The Prophet (p.b.u.h) recited (the Quran) aloud during the eclipse prayer and when he had finished the eclipse prayer he said the Takbir and bowed. When he stood straight from bowing he would say "Sami 'al-l-ahu Lyman hamidah Rabbana walaka-l-hamd." And he would again start reciting. In the eclipse prayer there are four bowing and four prostrations in two Rakat. Al-Auza'i and others said that they had heard Az-Zuhi from 'Ursa from 'Aisha saying, "In the life-time of Allah's Apostle the sun eclipsed, and he made a person to announce: 'Prayer in congregation.' He led the prayer and performed four bowing and four prostrations in two Rakat." Narrated Al-Walid that 'Abdur-Rahman bin Namir had informed him that he had heard the same. Ibn Shihab heard the same. Az-Zuhrl said, "I asked ('Ursa), 'What did your brother 'Abdullah bin AzZubair do? He prayed two Rakat (of the eclipse prayer) like the morning prayer, when he offered the (eclipse) prayer in Median.' 'Ursa replied that he had missed (i.e. did not pray according to) the Prophet's tradition." Sulaiman bin Kathir and Sufyan bin Husain narrated from Az-Zuhri that the prayer for the eclipse used to be offered with loud recitation.

notes: The selected digital paragraph contains printed references 1065 and 1066 in full, including the Awzai route, the Abd al-Rahman ibn Namir continuation, the later discussion and both closing corroborators. These remain one app occurrence with no invented suffix or lost printed passage.

The Khan comparison wrongly says he had finished the eclipse prayer where the Arabic says recitation, misspells narrator names, and damages the later heard-Ibn-Shihab construction. Its exact retained body is marked as damaged. The selected Arabic, both prints and Bewley retain recitation before the bowing.

The two complete four-bowings, two-rakahs and four-prostrations statements remain. Both Prophet honorifics and both Aishah Most High honorifics are retained. The opening uses the selected al-Walid rather than Brill’s expanded al-Walid ibn Muslim; Ibn Namir is not expanded in that opening route. Ibn Hajar specifies Namir’s vocalization separately in his commentary.

The modern print omits Aishah in the second chain where the selected source and Brill include her; it still prints a feminine honorific. This is recorded as an edition difference, not used to remove her from the selected chain. Brill adds qalat before the first report and reverses the order of the final two corroborator names; the selected order remains Sufyan then Sulayman.

The later informed me is retained without inserting a named al-Walid speaker absent from the selected wording. Ibn Hajar discusses the linked transmission routes; that explanation remains separate. The final corroboration is a transmission note and is not speech attributed to the Prophet.

The working rendering reads ma sana akhuka dhalik as Your brother did not do that, retaining that and the following statement that he prayed only two rakahs. The English comparisons frame the opening as a question. This syntactic choice is explicitly provisional, with independent Arabic and English review pending. The following he said remains unnamed, and the source’s Yes response is retained. No new question or explanation is inserted into the displayed report.
